questions.question: Why does a heavy metals wiki cover lithium at all?
questions.answer: Lithium is most relevant here as a metal used in medical therapy for mania and bipolar disorder. According to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], it is tied to the toxicology literature through its narrow therapeutic index and its range of toxic effects.

questions.question: What does it mean that lithium has a "narrow therapeutic index"?
questions.answer: A narrow therapeutic index means the gap between a helpful dose and a toxic dose is small. [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]] identifies this narrow margin as the main reason lithium's toxicity is a concern in the context of its use as a therapy.

questions.question: What kinds of health effects are associated with lithium toxicity?
questions.answer: The page reports that lithium toxicities involve neuromuscular, central nervous system, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, renal, and thyroid effects, per [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. The page does not provide dose thresholds or quantitative detail for these effects.

questions.question: How complete is the information on this lithium page right now?
questions.answer: This is a source-map stub created during the re-ingest of [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], and it currently rests on a single source. Substantive lithium-specific expansion is noted as awaiting a dedicated ingest, so detailed food or consumer-product exposure information is not yet covered.
